artifactType: Desktop app surface set: coding tool install and update management
audience: Developers using Trace on macOS to start Claude Code, Codex, Pi, Antigravity, and Cursor Composer sessions
fidelity: High-fidelity screen artifacts with local prototype interactions
primaryJob: Notice that a session tool is missing or out of date, then install or update it on the user's own initiative instead of being interrupted by an auto-opening dialog at launch
coreFlow: Trace starts with no dialog; the sidebar footer row reports coding tool state
User opens the popover deliberately from the sidebar row and sees the whole situation in place
The popover carries exactly one action per state, so most visits resolve without navigating
Anything per-tool hands off to Settings > Coding tools, the single full surface
Installed tools sit top level with one action each; Claude Code and Codex stay top level even when not installed
Tools that are not installed collapse into an Available to install accordion in Settings, and compress to one line in the popover
User runs Update all or a single install, watches inline progress, and resolves success or failure in whichever surface they started from
A missing tool is also caught contextually in the New session type picker

direction.name: Instrument panel
principles: Version numbers are the data: monospace, aligned, always showing current then target
Status is a glyph plus a label, never color alone
One primary action per group so actionable updates outrank absent tools
Absent tools are collapsed, not deleted, so the list never nags

references.source: User-supplied screenshot of the current Trace macOS window with the auto-opening 'Keep your coding tools ready' dialog
preserve: Near-black window background with a slightly lighter raised surface for panels and dialogs
Left sidebar information architecture: workspace switcher, Home, Inbox, CREATE group with Apps/Designs/Documents/Animations, Projects group, account row pinned to the bottom
Session list columns: Name, Type, Created by, Last message
Blue as the active navigation and focus accent
Tool set and their real state at capture time: Claude Code 2.1.220, Codex 0.144.5, Pi 0.74.0 up to date, Antigravity and Cursor Composer not installed
reinterpret: Replace the auto-opening centered modal with a user-initiated sidebar popover backed by a Settings page
Replace the five identical orange wrench icons with distinct monochrome per-tool marks that actually differentiate rows
Give the actions a hierarchy instead of five visually equal grey buttons
Group by installed versus not installed, and collapse the not-installed group
Show version transitions in monospace rather than proportional body text
avoidCopying: Claude, OpenAI, Pi, Antigravity, and Cursor logotypes or brand marks; marks are neutral geometric stand-ins
Any real user account identity beyond the sample name already visible in the capture
Exact pixel replication of the macOS title bar chrome
evidence: Window background reads as near-black #09090b and the dialog surface as roughly #18181b, matching the Trace Default neutrals already in tokens.css
Active sidebar item 'In Progress' and the focus ring on the Claude Code Update button are both blue, so secondary is set to #3b82f6
Dialog and button corners measure roughly 12px and 8px, so radius.surface is tightened from 16 to 12 while radius.control stays 8
Version strings in the capture already read as current then target ('Version 2.1.220 -> 2.1.222'), which the design promotes to monospace

assumptions: Trace performs installs and updates itself, so progress, cancel, and failure are designed inline rather than handing off to a terminal
Claude Code and Codex are first-class session types and stay top level regardless of install state, per explicit user direction
No auto-opening dialog and no Home banner: the passive signal is the sidebar row label plus a count badge, so the surface never interrupts
Two surfaces only, per explicit user direction: the sidebar popover and Settings > Coding tools. The docked side panel explored earlier was cut as redundant with Settings

The popover exposes exactly one action button per state; per-tool controls, install paths, logs, history, and removal live only in Settings. That division is what keeps the popover small enough to justify existing
Desktop control height is 32px rather than the 44px mobile touch minimum, keeping list density appropriate to a developer tool
